title: Choose Pocket of Stuff’s visual world
question: The physics-block mechanism stays fixed; choose the material world that should carry it.

options.label: The Toymaker’s Assembly Mat
options.lineage: screen-printed wooden toys, workshop registration marks, and color-study offcuts
options.thesis: A portfolio assembled by hand from imperfect colored pieces on a quiet maker’s surface.
options.viewport: A tall block tower occupies the working surface while a compact title, one-line instruction, and reset mark sit at its edges.
options.risk: It becomes childish if the grain, typography, and color wear are exaggerated.

raised.raise: Hover, grab, moved, and opened states each get one unmistakable visual rule.
Physics is damped and trustworthy rather than frantic or springy.
Reduced motion becomes a composed static construction, not a disabled version.
Every block keeps its project label attached through motion and rotation.

options.label: The Gallery Play Table
options.lineage: museum handling tables and modernist educational objects
options.thesis: The projects behave like collectible design objects in a calm, editorial exhibition.
options.viewport: A low plinth supports two balanced block clusters with generous white space and a precise exhibition caption.
options.risk: This is the familiar high-design portfolio answer and may sand away the oddness that makes the idea yours.

options.label: Weather Workshop
options.lineage: temporary architecture cut from clouds and sky voids
options.thesis: Each project is a soft block of weather, stacked briefly before the visitor releases it.
options.viewport: A pale tower is cut by deep-blue gaps, with projects identified like measured construction stock.
options.case: It matches the constructive physics unusually well, but visitors identify less strongly with clouds than with the wooden-toy idea you specified.
options.risk: The surreal material could make the projects feel like anonymous game pieces.

options.label: Block Arcade
options.thesis: Projects become bright tile sprites in a strict game-state grid.
options.viewport: A score-like header sits above a full-screen tile playfield.
options.case: The state language is excellent, but the arcade costume would overwhelm the personal work and discard the wooden material.
options.kept: Strict state discipline for hover, grab, moved, and opened blocks.
options.risk: It reads as a game portfolio template rather than Zach’s collection.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.lineage: damped aircraft gauges and trusted mechanical readings
options.thesis: Each project occupies one calm instrument whose movement exposes its state.
options.viewport: A fixed constellation of project instruments fills the page.
options.case: Its motion quality is strong, but gauges contradict the free-building interaction and personal tone.
options.kept: Damped, readable motion that settles quickly and predictably.
options.risk: It frames creative work as telemetry rather than objects worth exploring.

options.label: Kinetic Sand Rings
options.lineage: raised relief, warm gold glyphs, and rotational selection
options.thesis: Projects rise from a tactile field as the visitor turns a circular index.
options.viewport: A concentric project index rises around one central selection.
options.case: It offers beautiful material motion but replaces the requested tower and makes project count harder to scan.
options.kept: A deliberately composed reduced-motion state with no simulated grain animation.
options.risk: The visual system carries cultural specificity unrelated to the portfolio.

options.label: Color Lawn
options.lineage: saturated fields with floating white capsules
options.thesis: Blocks spill over one fearless color field while navigation floats above as detached objects.
options.viewport: An oversized title and block cast share a saturated stage.
options.case: Its confidence is useful, but the pill language competes with the block shapes and repeats a common current-web motif.
options.kept: One decisive ground color rather than a timid neutral gradient.
options.risk: The interface would date faster than the projects.

options.label: Project Provenance
options.lineage: archival custody ribbons and dated object labels
options.thesis: A continuous red thread links projects through time and ownership.
options.viewport: A single project history unrolls down the page.
options.case: The chronology is clear, but the linear reading order contradicts playful spatial discovery.
options.kept: Labels remain attached to objects and never become detached hover tooltips.
options.risk: It makes a young portfolio feel institutional and retrospective.

canonCard.label: The Conventional Portfolio Grid
canonCard.thesis: A highly polished white portfolio with project thumbnails arranged in a predictable responsive grid.
canonCard.viewport: A bold name, short introduction, and immediately scannable project grid.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to browse because it abandons the idea that makes the site memorable.
